To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
perceived course utility and satisfaction with the medium are the main factors determining distance learning course adoption.

(1) perceived course utility, (2) lack of mistrust of the institution, (3) satisfaction with the Internet and (4) the perceived usefulness of the Internet are the factors that influence the decision to do asynchronous distance learning courses.

the purchase intention of an asynchronous distance learning course is positively influenced by the utility that the student perceives in the distance learning course, the service considerations that the student perceieves in the course and the relation that the student has with the Internet when doing the course.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the factors that influence the decision of a student to do a distance training programme.
the study of the purchase intention of distance learning courses.
the study of factors influencing asynchronous distance course purchase intention in the Spanish market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Internet is a good vehicle for the development of asynchronous distance learning courses.

, in order to increase the number of students who enrol in distance learning courses, the main effort should be directed to the development and implementation of strategies that increase the course utility and the students satisfaction with Internet use when doing this kind of training.
, although the Internet is a powerful tool, it is not the key factor for the success of an asynchronous distance learning course.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decision to purchase distance learning courses is determined by the perceived usefulness of the course and the satisfaction with the use and the trust in the Internet.
the Internet has become the preferred medium to do distance training courses.
the decision to buy a distance learning course is determined by a set of factors related to the course and to the use of the Internet.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Internet and its related services are not the only factor that influences the purchase decision of an asynchronous distance learning course, but also the characteristics of the course, its perceived utility, and the service considerations of the institution organising the training.
companies should not forget that distance learning students are not a homogeneous group, but a heterogeneous one.
companies should be aware of the importance of the Internet in the purchase decision of distance learning courses.
